physicalEvidence.status: Current directed IHMC/UWF group, learned perception coupled to real humanoid tasks;2024 experiments/2026 journal issue
physicalEvidence.summary: The full November 2024 manuscript, later published in the 2026 journal volume, integrates retrained YOLOv8 handle segmentation, depth and planar-region estimation into real Nadia door traversal. Learned poses feed behavior authoring/execution; operator-authored behavior trees and model-based whole-body control generate motion, rather than an end-to-end learned motion policy. Trials cover multiple push/pull mechanisms and composite sequences. The humanoid is hydraulically tethered, uses mock door frames with real hardware, and relies on human grasp/footstep tuning. These are demonstrated physical tasks, not an unrestricted field deployment. Current IHMC roster independently names Griffin PI/team lead and includes coauthors/ISR students. Physical25;2026 issue date does not mean the experiments were first performed in 2026. A separate March 2026 advised H1-2 project executes a proprioception-only PPO recovery policy at 50 Hz through low-level PD. All ten trials reached upright, but three then required safety intervention; its 93.4% figure is simulation. This supports current directed learned-action work while preserving the earlier door-experiment chronology.
